objections.claim: The no-listener startup mechanism has an unresolved bootstrap cycle. A Node-based `pylae` entrypoint cannot sanitize `NODE_OPTIONS=--inspect…` before Node processes it, so the prohibited listener can open before launcher code runs. A pre-Node shell/env launcher instead executes an interpreter outside the closed external-tool set and cannot perform the required node-binary open/hash/same-fd execution using the stated in-process `node:crypto` mechanism. Thus no specified supported entrypoint simultaneously satisfies startup sanitization, complete executable-closure confinement, and mutation-point-bound Node identity; the NODE_OPTIONS regression would not discriminate a compliant installation from this gap.

The Node-version prose oracle is self-referential as specified. It scans ALL tracked text while `node-version-claims.json` must store each hit's literal `matched_text`. Recording an exception such as `Node 18+` creates the same sub-22.12 hit inside the inventory; inventorying that hit creates another occurrence indefinitely. Without a structurally defined exclusion or non-matching canonical encoding for inventory payload fields, the exact-current inventory cannot reach a finite fixed point, so the reconciliation oracle is unsatisfiable whenever an exception exists.

The archive-install acceptance contract is internally contradictory. It requires out-of-artifact digest, attestation-identity, and trust-root verification—and a recorded receipt—before any archive byte is extracted or executed, with `pylae doctor` refusing `unverified-install` without that receipt. It simultaneously requires a clean-room job to extract first and requires the archive-mode offline subset to go green from the tarball alone while reporting `publisher-unverified`. A tarball alone cannot supply the mandatory external receipt or satisfy the pre-extraction ordering; the clean-room oracle therefore cannot meet both stated acceptance conditions.
